Implementation Plan Implementation plan for the security finding `inline-remote-config-bypasses-merged-pr-guard` (Refs #3576) Planning ref: `claude/sync-pr-merge-guard-twin` at `c9de2b91ee58275c20371933b6028d0434172190`. This matches the integration branch named in the issue (`Integration branch mismatch: false`), so the fix PR targets `claude/sync-pr-merge-guard-twin`. Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends _guarded_git_invocations / _push_targets / _git_environment / _run in .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py Scope-mode justification: The finding is about one defect class: git configuration given inline with the command changes what `git push` does, but the guard reads only on-disk config. The plan closes every instance of that class that is in the same code path. That means `-c` (the reported case), `--config-env` (which currently stops the guard from seeing the push at all, see C2), and inline `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment assignments. It does not change how the guard handles on-disk config, the MCP push path, or the `gh` lookups. Handling `--config-env` and the env-var forms as well costs about 30 extra lines and adds no dependency or external interface. Leaving them out would leave a reproducible bypass. Per §6, security comes before minimal change, so the complete option is chosen. ## Automation / wiring (§20.E) - No new script. The change extends an existing hook in place. - Entry point: the existing `PreToolUse` hook on `Bash` in `.claude/settings.json` and in `workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json`. Both are unchanged. Consumers receive the template copy through the existing `@stable` sync (`update_workflows.yml`). - No long-running supervisor, no database work, and no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`. ## Problem (verified against the code at this ref) I reproduced the exploit with a local bare remote using `git push --dry-run --porcelain`. Git 2.55 pushes `refs/heads/feature:refs/heads/feature` for: `git -c remote.main.url= -c push.default=current push --repo=origin main` The guard handles the same command like this: 1. `_guarded_git_invocations` (around lines 347-433) skips `-c ` because `-c` is in `GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS_WITH_VALUE`, and then throws the value away. 2. `_push_targets` (around lines 451-541) sees `--repo=origin`, so `remote_provided` is true. It then runs `git config --get remote.main.url` with no inline config. That returns exit code 1, so the code takes `refspecs = positionals` (the line `refspecs = positionals[1:] if code == 0 else positionals`, around line 500). As a result, `main` is treated as a refspec. 3. In `_evaluate_bash` (around lines 1316-1446), `branch == base` (`main`) hits the `continue`. The merged-PR check never runs for the branch actually being pushed. Related instances found while checking the code: - **C1.** Every helper lookup ignores inline config: `repo_slug` (`remote.origin.url`), `current_branch`, `default_branch` (`ls-remote origin`), and the history-fallback fetches. So `-c remote.origin.url=…` also changes which repo the guard queries. - **C2.** `--config-env` is not in `GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS_WITH_VALUE`. For `git --config-env remote.main.url=U push …`, both `git_subcommands` and `_guarded_git_invocations` take `remote.main.url=U` to be the subcommand, so the push is not guarded at all. I confirmed git accepts the separate-argument form. - **C3.** Inline environment variables (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, `GIT_CONFIG`) inject config the same way `-c` does. The guard only reads `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` from inline assignments. ## Files likely to change 1. `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: the fix. 2. `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: must stay a byte-identical copy of file 1 (`test_template_copies_are_identical`, `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:1293`). 3. `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`: new regression tests. 4. `changelog.d/6336-pr-merge-guard-inline-git-config.md`: new changelog fragment (CLAUDE.md §20). `CHANGELOG.md` is not edited. No change to `CLAUDE.md`, its template twin, `agents.md`, or the settings files. The §21.B description of the guard's conditions stays accurate. ## Functions / modules to implement (all in `pr_merge_status_guard.py`) 1. **Constants** - Add `"--config-env"` to `GIT_GLOBAL_OPTS_WITH_VALUE`. This fixes subcommand detection in `git_subcommands` and `_guarded_git_invocations`. - New `_INLINE_GIT_CONFIG_ENV_RE`: matches `GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_(COUNT|PARAMETERS|GLOBAL|SYSTEM|NOSYSTEM)`, and `GIT_CONFIG_(KEY|VALUE)_\d+`. - New `_GIT_CONFIG_ARGS: ContextVar[tuple[str, ...]]`, default `()`. 2. **NamedTuples.** Append trailing fields with defaults so all existing positional and keyword construction keeps working: - `_GitInvocation.config: tuple[str, ...] = ()` holds the ordered `-c` values. - `_GitInvocation.config_block: str = ""` holds the reason when inline config cannot be resolved. - `_GuardTarget.config: tuple[str, ...] = ()`. 3. **`_guarded_git_invocations`** - Leading-assignment loop: an assignment (or `+=`) whose name matches `_INLINE_GIT_CONFIG_ENV_RE` sets `config_block = "inline environment override"`. - Global-option loop: - `-c `: append `v` to `config`. If `v` contains `$` or a backtick, set `config_block`, because shell expansion means the key or value is unknown. - `--config-env ` and `--config-env=`: always set `config_block`, because the value comes from an environment variable the hook cannot see. - Keep the existing `-C`, `--git-dir` and `--work-tree` handling unchanged. Do not route config values through the `_literal_guard_path` loop, which must keep handling only `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE`. - Pass `config` and `config_block` into `_GitInvocation`. 4. **`_git_environment(overrides, config=())`**: also set and reset `_GIT_CONFIG_ARGS`. The new parameter is keyword-optional, so existing callers are unchanged. 5. **`_run`**: when `_GIT_CONFIG_ARGS` is not empty, insert `-c ` pairs right after the first `argv` element equal to `"git"`. This also covers the `env GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git ls-remote …` form. With empty config, `argv` is unchanged, which keeps the existing tests that match exact `argv` working. `gh` invocations never get the pairs. This resolves C1: every lookup now sees the same config the real command would. 6. **New helper `_inline_push_config_block(config) -> str`**: a lexical check that needs no subprocess. Section and key names are compared case-insensitively. It returns a reason if any inline key is one the guard does not model: - `remote..push`, `remote..mirror`, `remote..pushurl` - any `url.*` key (`insteadOf` / `pushInsteadOf`) - `include.*` or `includeIf.*` - a key without a `.` 7. **`_push_targets`** - First: if `invocation.config_block` is set, or `_inline_push_config_block(invocation.config)` returns a reason, return one `_GuardTarget(..., warning="inline git config: ")` marked as blocking (see 8). - Run the positional-repository probe (`git config --get remote.

.url`) inside `_git_environment(invocation.environment, invocation.config)`. This is the core fix: `main` is now recognised as the repository. - New no-refspec branch, only when `invocation.config` is not empty: resolve the effective `push.default` with `git config --get push.default` (inline config applied; exit code 1 means `simple`; any other non-zero code blocks). - `simple`, `current`: existing behaviour (current branch). - `nothing`: `[]`. - `matching`: bulk `"push.default=matching"` (existing confirmation path). - `upstream`, `tracking`: resolve `branch..merge`. A `refs/heads/` value targets `` through `_branch_ref`; anything else blocks. - any other value: blocks. - Every `_GuardTarget` built here carries `config=invocation.config`. - Non-push invocations in `_evaluate_bash` get `config` as well. 8. **`_evaluate_bash`** - Use `_git_environment(target.environment, target.config)` for every lookup, including the `rev-parse` source check. - A target whose warning starts with `"inline git config:"` is appended to `blocks` (exit 2) with this message: `BLOCKED: git uses inline Git configuration the merged-PR guard cannot resolve (). Re-run without the inline override, or set it in the repository config first.` - For `commit` invocations with `config_block` set, add the same block. Inline config can redirect `remote.origin.url`, and with it the repo the guard queries. - All other paths are unchanged. ## Data structures affected - `_GitInvocation` and `_GuardTarget` get new trailing fields with defaults (additive). - A new ContextVar. - No changes to the cache format, JSON output shape, or log text of existing messages. ## API / interface changes - New block message (exit 2) for unresolvable inline config. - Hook input and output schema unchanged. No environment variables added or renamed. - `CLAUDE_PR_MERGE_GUARD` still disables the guard. ## Decisions ### D1 — Apply inline config by re-passing `-c` to the guard's own git calls - Chosen: store the parsed `-c` values on the invocation and target, and have `_run` prepend them to each `git` argv through a ContextVar set by `_git_environment`. - Alternatives considered: - Translate the values into `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE` environment entries. Git releases before 2.31 ignore these silently, so the guard would fail open. - Lexically special-case `remote.

.url` keys only. This misses the slug lookup and `push.default`. - Why: passing the same `-c` arguments makes each lookup see exactly the config git uses for the real command, on any git version, and covers every lookup in one place. ### D2 — Unresolvable inline config is denied (exit 2), not asked - Chosen: block wh
